counterevidence_considered.description: Each k1 code (u01 through u06) appears exactly twice — for example u01 on the first two data rows — which is the pattern that would demonstrate the issue if k1 were established as a unit identifier for the `a` measurements. This is the strongest evidence against my verdict, but the task affirmatively withholds that identification, so the repetition of an opaque code does not demonstrate repeated entry of the same source unit.

evidence.description: The governing task explicitly states that k1 and k2 are opaque codes and that the task does not establish whether either code identifies a source item, so a repeated k1 code cannot, from the visible files, be shown to be a repeated entry of the same source unit.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items measured by columns `a` and `b`. Treat `k1` and `k2` as opaque codes; `tag` is an opaque annotation. This task does not establish whether either code identifies a source item within either collection. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the items represented in that row.

evidence.description: The workflow applies ttest_ind to all rows and the report's df of 22 matches the 12 rows per side; nothing in the workflow or report itself establishes that any single source unit was entered more than once.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to overturn the no-issue verdict by treating the doubled k1 codes as evidence of repeated units entering ttest_ind. The attempt fails on the task's own terms: the task instructs that the codes are opaque and expressly states it does not establish that either code identifies a source item, and the instruction not to guess unstated intentions bars me from inferring that identity. Without a visible-file basis linking repeated codes to repeated source units, the issue class is not demonstrated; the suspicious pattern remains a concern outside what these files can establish.
